rv.q: "The Book of Mormon" is still delivering side-splitting hilarity with its impeccable blend of catchy songs, biting satire, and nothing-is-off-limits humor.
Fifteen years after its Broadway debut, The Book of Mormon remains one of the funniest musicals ever written.
If you haven't seen The Book of Mormon, go see it.

If you're at all curious about the show, this is a great cast to see for this tour, with a fun production, some epically hilarious moments, and a lot of well done songs — and performances that aren't just crude, but even have a touch of heart.
This cast makes it all look so fun.
The cast is great, especially understudy Rayna J. who played Nabulungi on June 2nd, her strong beautiful voice working perfectly in the goofy ballads given to her.
The cast is full of skilled singers, like Charity Arianna (Nabulungi), as well as talented comedic actors, such as Jacob Aune (Cunningham).
I'm happy to say that it's just as sharp, funny, and daring as the hype promised it would be.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this irreverent musical's enduring brilliance, praising its catchy songs, biting satire, and side-splitting humor that still resonates 15 years after its debut, with audiences leaping to their feet in approval.
